01 / The core

Coordination and communication, without a monolith.

Mycelium and Unibus are the core relationship. Each remains useful on its own; provider-neutral adapters let them cooperate without embedding one inside the other.

MFleet coordination

Mycelium

Maps what exists, establishes who may act, and delivers verified software safely across a heterogeneous fleet.

  • Topology, devices, services, and resources
  • Peer identity, role-based access, and SSH
  • Signed, content-addressed distribution
  • Planned activation, health checks, and rollback evidence
narrow adapters
UEndpoint communication

Unibus

Supplies authorized inter-device messaging plus stream and service discovery between independently useful endpoints.

  • Application messaging and event transport
  • Provider-neutral discovery integration
  • Stream and service announcements
  • Local or routed deployment without fleet ownership
Native transports stay native. Applications do not all have to speak Unibus. It can describe or discover an H.264, MIDI, RTSP, or other endpoint while media continues over its purpose-built transport. Mycelium does not absorb Unibus, and Unibus does not become the fleet database.
02 / Profiles

One base. Five deliberate jobs.

Profiles are derived capability sets—not separate distributions. Every optional application is selected by policy and retains its own lifecycle boundary.

Base

Debian minbase, systemd-networkd, SSH, hardware discovery, Mycelium identity and signed updates. No media, inference, or workload application.

Built + inspected
Edge

Adds native Canvas compositor dependencies and Unibus for an interactive on-premises node. Canvas and Unibus remain optional signed applications.

QEMU demonstrated
Headless edge

Adds Unibus runtime dependencies without a graphical session, Canvas, Xorg, or Weston. The current Pi image uses this userspace profile.

Image inspected
Compute

Explicit roles may select UMIE and Yggdrasil for accelerators, or Shroud for workload nodes. GPU discovery never grants placement authority.

GPU handoff proven
Cloud

Adds native Shroud workload dependencies without Canvas, Unibus, models, or credentials. Nested Firecracker boot is proven; a cloud-provider image is not.

Nested KVM proven

Standard selection

Planned

Excludes AGPL application packages by default. It still contains Debian and upstream software under GPL, LGPL, and other licenses; it is not “copyleft-free.”

With AGPL applications

Explicit opt-in · planned

Adds selected AGPL product applications under their own package licenses, source, and notices. This selection is orthogonal to base, edge, compute, and cloud hardware profiles.

These are package-selection variants, not released images and not a relicensing of third-party software.

04 / Values

Infrastructure should serve its operators—not strand them.

P—01⌁

Open at the core

First-party foundational primitives target MIT or Apache-2.0. Assembled distributions retain every upstream package’s own license.

P—02⟲

Right to repair

Modular drivers and portable contracts keep old machines supportable after a vendor moves on.

P—03◇

Private by design

Local-first operation, least privilege, signed changes, and explicit evidence—without a permanent cloud dependency.

P—04⋈

Interoperable

Linux, macOS, Windows, embedded systems, and vendor appliances participate through narrow contracts, not forced rewrites.

05 / Operator docs

Automation that still has a manual runbook.

The current documentation starts with reproducible rootfs assembly and verification. Installation is experimental; no public image should be trusted merely because it boots.

Getting started

Build a minimal rootfs

Resolve capability-owned package lists from the shared base, then assemble the architecture and profile you need.

cd fungOS/base ./scripts/check.sh sudo ./scripts/build.sh amd64 edge
Build prerequisites & runbook
Verification

Inspect before boot

Validate required files, blank machine identity, package closure, and the output digest before a rootfs enters a boot workflow.

cd fungOS/base sudo ./scripts/inspect.sh \ out/fungos-edge-amd64.tar cd out sha256sum -c fungos-edge-amd64.tar.sha256
Pi hardware, flashing & first boot
Enrollment

Create identity on first contact

Images contain no cloned peer identity or enrollment secret. Issue a short-lived claim, transfer it over an authenticated channel, and let Mycelium consume it only after successful enrollment.

  1. Verify the SSH host key independently.
  2. Transfer an owner-only peer claim.
  3. Run mycelium setup --claim-file ….
  4. Confirm daemon identity and remove the bootstrap copy.
Enrollment instructions
Safe updates

Plan, stage, verify, recover

Signed manifests select content-addressed bytes. Native service adapters own restart and health. Failed activation returns to a checked previous version and persists the result.

mycelium software plan POLICY.json --json mycelium software policy set POLICY.json --write mycelium software auto-run --json
Updates, health & recovery runbook
Architecture

Keep ownership boring

Genesis installs. Mycelium operates machines. Unibus transports authorized messages. Canvas composes interfaces. Shroud executes workloads. UMIE and Yggdrasil remain optional compute applications.

Component ownership
Security boundary

Discovery is not authority

A resource observation can nominate a GPU, camera, service, or storage device. It cannot grant a workload, person, or service permission to use it.

Profiles & security boundaries

07 / Where it grows

One operating philosophy. Very different rooms.

The substrate is shared; each environment keeps the tools, policies, hardware, and native transports that make it distinct.

Manufacturing

Shops that can own their stack

Keep control systems supportable, segment shop-floor networks, and build toward auditable lifecycle management without binding operations to a disappearing vendor.

CNC application work is future userspace, not shipped capability
Recording studios

Connect MIDI without rebuilding the room

Puget Audio is the design-partner environment: mixed-generation Macs, Pis, interfaces, MIDI devices, and native low-latency media transports.

Active design and deployment environment
Homelab + on-prem

Make the weird fleet coherent

Map networks, manage access, distribute software, and integrate the FOSS services you already trust.

Mycelium foundation active
Shared institutions

Many users. Clear boundaries.

Universities, companies, and nonprofits need role-based access, privacy boundaries, evidence, and graceful disconnected operation.

Identity and policy primitives evolving
High assurance

Evidence before checkboxes

Open profiles can express STIG-aligned controls and collect evidence. Accreditation, authorization, and organization-specific compliance remain separate processes.

Enablement, not certification
08 / Trust boundaries

Security claims should be inspectable.

The open core includes profile authoring, enforcement, application, evidence, and community or FPL-published open baselines. Enterprise value is maintained, validated and signed profile releases, regression testing, mappings, implementation guidance, tailored qualification, and support—not a paywall around basic security.

IdentityPeople, machines, and services remain distinct principals.
AuthorityRole-based grants define action; discovery never grants trust.
ChangeSigned inputs, deterministic plans, rollback checks, and durable receipts.
LicensingFirst-party primitives target MIT/Apache-2.0; Linux, Debian, Pi firmware, and other packages retain their own licenses.
AssuranceNo current image is certified, accredited, or approved for regulated or classified operation.
Build in public

A substrate that can outlive its first vendor.

The current public upstream is ajmwagar/mycelium. Future Present Labs is developing the wider fungOS direction while keeping component ownership and licensing explicit.
